SPECIAL SOUTH GATE CITY COUNCIL
  SPECIAL SOUTH GATE CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

  Tuesday, June 24, 2025 at 5:00 p.m.

  SOUTH GATE COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  8650 CALIFORNIA AVE
  SOUTH GATE, CA 90280

  VIEW MEETING LIVE ONLINE AT:
  HTTPS://YOUTUBE.COM/@SOUTHGATECA90280
City Officials
MAYOR, Maria Davila  CITY CLERK, Yodit Glaze
VICE MAYOR, Joshua Barron  CITY TREASURER, Jose De La Paz
COUNCIL MEMBER, Maria del Pilar Avalos  CITY MANAGER, Rob Houston
COUNCIL MEMBER, Gil Hurtado  CITY ATTORNEY, Raúl F. Salinas
COUNCIL MEMBER, Al Rios

If you would like to participate in this meeting, you can participate via the following
options:

1. VIEW THE MEETING LIVE ONLINE AT: https://youtube.com/@SouthGateCA90280
Please allow up to 24 hours after the meeting for the archive to be available.
2. PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING by emailing the City Clerk at:
yglaze@sogate.org no later than 4:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please write
"Public Comment" in the subject line.
3. ATTEND THE MEETING IN PERSON
*The disruption in service of any alternative method does not prelude the City Council
or other legislative
body from taking further action and moving forward on the agenda.

Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,
closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business

  1
 session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 4:00 pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be
summarized by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City
Council and will also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be
recorded for public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Call to Order/Roll Call

CALL TO ORDER:  Maria Davila, Mayor
ROLL CALL:  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

Open Session

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers first. After all speakers in the Chambers have spoken,
the Presiding Officer will call upon those participating via zoom or teleconference.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, virtually, email, phone call, mail and any other method which may become
available. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such times when a State of
Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

  4
 STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email
at yglaze@sogate.org.

  P R O C L A  Ml A  T  ffi U  H

WHEREAS,  all residents  in the City  of South  Gate deserve  to be treated  with
  dignity, respect,  and equality,  regardless  of their  sexual  orientation  or
  gender  identity;  and

WHEREAS,  LGBTQ+  Pride  Month  is a time to reflect  on the challenges  faced by
  LGBTQ+  individuals  throughout  history,  and to honor  those who have
  fought-and  continue  to fight-for  equality  and justice;  and

WHEREAS,  Pride Month  also serves as a celebration  of identity,  visibility,  and self-
  worth.  In South  Gate, we recognize  and value  the contributions  of
  LGBTQ+  residents  who help make our city stronger,  more  diverse,  and
  more  inclusive;  and

WHEREAS,  our community  joins  others  across the nation  in reaffirming  the rights
  and freedoms  of LGBTQ+  individuals,  and in standing  against
  discrimination  in all its forms;  and

WHEREAS,  LGBTQ+  individuals  are represented  at all levels  of society,  including
  in public  service  and civic  leadership,  and their presence  continues  to
  inspire  positive  change  in communities  like ours; and

WHEREAS,  during  Pride Month,  we celebrate  the courage  and determination  of
  those who live authentically  and openly  in the face of adversity,  and
  we commit  ourselves  to building  a community  that embraces  everyone,
  regardless  of who they love or how they identify.

NOW,  THEREFORE,  be it proclaimed  on this 24th  day of June,  2025,  that I, Maria
Davila,  Mayor  of the City  of South  Gate,  on behalf  of the City  Council,  do hereby
declare  June 2025 as LGBTQ+  Pride  Month  in the City  of South  Gate, and encourage
all residents  to celebrate  our diversity  and to continue  advancing  equity,  inclusion,  and
justice  for all.

  41
   Item No. 3

  P R O) C L A  M  A  T  fi @ N

WHEREAS,  the month  of June serves as a reminder  of the remarkable  resilience  of the
  human mind,  as well as its vulnerabilities.  It affirms  that experiencing
  emotional  distress is a natural  part of being human-and  unlike  machines,
  we possess not only the capacity  to feel deeply,  but also the ability  to heal,
  especially  when we support  one another;  and

WHEREAS,  traiuna  can present  in many forms. "Big  T" trauma  refers to events
  involving  actual or threatened  death or serious injury,  such as war,  natural
  disasters,  or physical  assault. "Small  T" trauma  arises from  distressing  but
  non-life-threatening  experiences,  including  divorce,  financial  hardship,  or

  sudden relocation;  and

WHEREAS,  while  some individuals  recover  from post-traumatic  stress within  weeks
  or months,  others may experience  long-term  symptoms  requiring  extended
  care. PTSD  is a highly  treatable  condition;  however,  stigma and lack of
  awareness  often prevent  individuals  from  seeking the help they need; and

WHEREAS,  National  PTSD Awareness  Month  aims to break down those barriers  by
  educating  the public,  reducing  stigma,  and promoting  effective  treatments
  such as counseling,  support  groups,  and medication;  and

WHEREAS,  open dialogue  about PTSD  encourages  understanding  and compassion,
  making  it more likely  that those affected  will  reach out for support.  The
  journey  to recovery  is unique  for everyone,  but healing  is always possible.

NOW,  THEREFORE,  be it proclaimed  on this 24th day of June,  2025, that I, Maria
Davila,  Mayor  of the City  of South  Gate,  on behalf  of the City Council,  do hereby  declare
June 2025 as National  Post-Traumatic  Stress Disorder  Awareness  Month  and urge all
citizens  to learn about the signs, symptoms,  and treatment  options  available  to support  those
living  with PTSD  and other mental  health  challenges.

  42
   Item No. 4

  P R a C L A  Ml A  T  ll a  N

  on July 4, 1776,  the Continental  Congress  formally  adopted  the
  Declaration  of Independence,  marking  the birth  of the United
  States  of  America  and  affirming  the  nation's  founding
  principles  of liberty,  democracy,  and justice  for all; and

  Independence  Day is a time  for Americans  to come together  in
  unity  and pride  to celebrate  the enduring  spirit  of freedom  and
  the  sacrifices  made  by  generations  of individuals  who  have
  defended  and upheld  the values  on whichthis  country  was built;
  and

  the City  of South  Gate proudly  joins  communities  across  the
  nation  in celebrating  this historic  day with  festivities  that honor
  our  nation's  heritage,  encourage  civic  pride,  and  bring
  neighbors,  families,  and friends  together;  and

  the City  of South  Gate's  annual  4th of July Independence  Day
  Celebration  is a cherished  traditionthat  features  family-friendly
  activities,  live  entertainment,  food  vendors,  and a spectacular
  fireworks  show,  fostering  a strong  sense  of community  and
  shared celebration;  and

  this year's  celebration  on Friday,  July  4, 2025,  continues  that
  tradition  by providing  a safe, inclusive,  and joyful  space  for
  residents  and visitors  of all ages to reflect  on our freedoms  and
  look  ahead with  hope and unity.

NOW,  THEREFORE,  I, Maria  Davila,  Mayor  of the City  of South  Gate,  on
behalf  of the City  Council,  do hereby  proclaim  July  4, 2025, as Independence  Day
in the City  of South  Gate,  and call upon  all residents  to join  in cornmemorating
this day with  pride,  gratitude,  and cornrnunity  spirit.

  South  Gate employee  was involved  in a rear-end  collision  and the claim  is

  being  the city and the employee.
  made against  On a motion made by

  Item 1(c) is a claim  against  the city arising  from  a pothole  on the 710 on-

  ramp.  That on-ramp  is not part of the City  of South  Gate and on a motion
  made by Councilwoman  Avalos and seconded  by Vice Mayor  Barron  and

  on a vote of 5-0, the City of South Gate authorized  the defense  of that

  lawsuit.
